audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[].side read 'Skill' on all seven rows, content win[] read 'Ekko' on all seven, and the content whys[] under those rows said the opposite of the row — whys[0] 'Lux's Q range means she dictates the trade, not you', whys[2] 'it's still her lane to press', both sitting under a row labelled Ekko.
audit.why: The kit settles the early rows: Light Binding is 1175 and Lucent Singularity 1100, both past Ekko's 1075 Q, and Ekko's E closes only 325 — Lux genuinely owns levels 1-3. From 4-5 a dodged flat-10s Q claws it even, and 6 onward Chronobreak plus a dashless target hands it to Ekko, exactly as whys[3..6] already say.
audit.corrected: Both layers set to Lux, Lux, Lux, Skill, Ekko, Ekko, Ekko — proposed as matched full/content pairs on every row — with the full-layer whys rewritten to match and the existing content whys left alone because they already describe this verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: content 'mid' told the reader to track her ultimate at 'roughly 20s+'.
audit.why: Final Spark is 60/50/40 — three times that at rank 1, which changes the whole post-ult punish window.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the real 60s at rank 1, and the same number added to breakdown.cooldowns and phases[4].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] called the shield 'Shield (E)'. The Illumination interaction was absent from the whole matchup.
audit.why: Prismatic Barrier is her W (12/11.5/11/10.5/10); E is Lucent Singularity, a slow zone she detonates. Illumination charges you off any damaging spell and her NEXT AUTO ignites it — so the auto-attack wind-up after her E, not the spell cast, is the cue to step out.
audit.corrected: Shield reassigned to Prismatic Barrier and Illumination written into dontsFull[0].d and dontsFull[2].d.

audit.why: Light Binding is a flat 10s at every rank — the single most useful number in this lane, because one dodge buys the full ten seconds — and Final Spark is 60s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Both written in, with the same sequencing repeated in dosFull[1].d and phases[3].why.

edits.before: From level 3 onward, bait her Q by faking a walk-up then punishing the miss with Q-E-AA. Level 6 flips the lane hard: her Final Spark all-in into your death is now the thing that gets her killed, since Chronobreak heals you off the damage and can burst her back. Roam together with jungle when she pushes to farm from range; she has zero mobility to escape a 2-man dive. Track her ult cooldown (roughly 20s+) — punish the window right after she uses it on a wave or a roam.
edits.after: From level 3 onward, bait her Q by faking a walk-up then punishing the miss with Q-E-AA — Light Binding is a flat 10s at every rank. Level 6 flips the lane hard: her Final Spark all-in into your death is now the thing that gets her killed, since Chronobreak heals you off the damage and can burst her back. Roam with your jungler when she pushes to farm from range; she has zero mobility to escape a 2-man dive. Final Spark is 60s at rank 1 — the window right after she spends it is yours.

notes: LEVEL CHART — READ THIS ONE. Three sources disagreed here: full phases[].side said Skill on all seven rows, content win[] said Ekko on all seven, and the content whys[] sitting under those Ekko rows explicitly said Lux owns levels 1-3 ('she dictates the trade, not you', 'still her lane to press'). Rather than propagate a row that argues with its own sentence, I set BOTH layers to Lux, Lux, Lux, Skill, Ekko, Ekko, Ekko — the reading the existing whys and the kit ranges both support (Q 1175 / E 1100 / W 1150 against Ekko's 1075 Q and 325 E). Rows 0-3 are proposed as matched full+content pairs; rows 4-6 needed a full-layer edit only because win[] already read Ekko there. This is the one row-set in my slice where I moved the content layer, and it moves AWAY from the packet levelChart (all Ekko) — flagged in questionsForUser in case the packet is meant to be authoritative over the prose. Also fixed: content 'mid' told the reader Final Spark is 'roughly 20s+' when it is 60/50/40, and wants.foe[2] called Prismatic Barrier 'Shield (E)'.
